summary:
NOX MED is an integrated astronaut health monitoring platform developed by NOX — New Orbit Exploration for long-duration space missions.

Our solution transforms isolated blood gas measurements into longitudinal physiological intelligence, combining acid-base parameters, electrolytes, lactate, and hemoglobin with wearable vital signs and spacecraft environmental telemetry.

Through personalized baselines, interactive trends, and explainable clinical observations, NOX MED helps astronauts recognize physiological changes, assess their health status, and identify findings requiring medical review.

The platform also provides mission-specific crew health profiles, spacecraft environmental monitoring, and interactive emergency simulations demonstrating how respiratory or metabolic abnormalities may evolve during spaceflight.

Designed around existing point-of-care diagnostic technologies, NOX MED introduces a device-independent approach to medical monitoring that could support greater crew autonomy during missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

Our prototype demonstrates these capabilities using synthetic mission data, establishing a foundation for future clinical validation and integration with space-qualified diagnostic systems.
details:
NOX MED — Mission Health Intelligence

The Challenge

Long-duration space exploration introduces significant medical challenges. Astronauts experience physiological adaptations associated with microgravity, radiation exposure, isolation, and changing environmental conditions. During missions to the Moon and Mars, communication delays and limited medical resources make autonomous health assessment increasingly important.

Traditional point-of-care diagnostic instruments provide valuable clinical measurements, but isolated results do not necessarily reveal how an astronaut's physiological condition evolves throughout a mission.

NOX MED addresses this challenge by transforming individual medical measurements into continuous longitudinal health awareness.

Our Solution

NOX MED is an integrated, web-based astronaut health monitoring prototype developed by NOX — New Orbit Exploration.

The platform combines three complementary information systems:

1. Blood Gas Intelligence — Our Core Innovation

NOX MED analyzes longitudinal trends in blood gases and biochemical measurements, including pH, pCO₂, pO₂, bicarbonate, base excess, lactate, electrolytes, glucose, hemoglobin, and oxygen saturation.

Inspired by point-of-care diagnostic systems such as the Radiometer ABL90 series, the platform is designed to transform intermittent laboratory results into clinically interpretable trends.

Rather than evaluating every measurement independently, NOX MED compares results against individual physiological baselines, previous measurements, and relevant reference intervals.

An explainable clinical rules framework helps identify potentially significant physiological changes, including acid-base disturbances, electrolyte abnormalities, and alterations in oxygenation.

Measurement quality, sample type, and analyzer reliability are considered to reduce misleading interpretations.

2. Integrated Astronaut Health Monitoring

NOX MED combines laboratory measurements with wearable-derived indicators such as heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, sleep, and physical activity.

An interactive anatomical interface allows operators to explore relevant physiological systems and access individual astronaut medical histories, measurements, and longitudinal health trends.

The platform supports astronaut self-assessment and medical review workflows, helping crew members recognize changes that may require additional evaluation.

3. Mission and Spacecraft Environmental Intelligence

NOX MED incorporates an interactive multi-mission navigation system, allowing operators to select different missions and review their assigned crew and spacecraft status.

Spacecraft environmental monitoring includes cabin carbon dioxide, oxygen, atmospheric pressure, temperature, humidity, and radiation exposure.

The system distinguishes astronaut health from spacecraft environmental and engineering status while allowing related observations to be examined together.

Technology and Development

NOX MED was developed as a web application using modern technologies, including React, Next.js, TypeScript, and interactive data visualization tools.

The project incorporates mission visualization, structured physiological data, longitudinal charts, and rule-based clinical observations.

AI-assisted development tools, including OpenAI ChatGPT, OpenAI Codex, and Anthropic Claude, supported software implementation, architectural planning, design refinement, and technical documentation.

The prototype uses fictional mission scenarios and synthetic physiological measurements to demonstrate its functionality.

Innovation and Creativity

NOX MED's central innovation is the integration of laboratory diagnostics, longitudinal physiological analysis, and spacecraft environmental information within a single mission-aware medical platform.

The project goes beyond conventional vital-sign dashboards by emphasizing intermittent blood sample interpretation, personalized physiological baselines, measurement quality, and explainable clinical observations.

An interactive emergency simulator demonstrates how changes in blood gas measurements may be recognized and reviewed during a developing medical event.

Its device-independent architecture is intended to accommodate different diagnostic instruments as future capabilities become available.

Intended Impact

NOX MED aims to support safer, more autonomous medical monitoring during long-duration missions.

By making physiological trends understandable and clinically contextualized, the platform could help astronauts and medical personnel recognize significant changes earlier, organize medical information, and support informed decisions when specialized assistance from Earth is delayed.

The long-term vision is a persistent astronaut health intelligence system connecting preflight, inflight, and postflight medical records across multiple missions.

NOX MED is currently a research and demonstration prototype. Operational use would require clinical validation, secure integration with medical systems, and appropriate spaceflight qualification.

NOX MED — Detect the change before it becomes an emergency.
